checks.title: A mail app logs in with a generated password from the platform secret, and no credential is left in stored state
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A person's mail app logs in with a generated password
  Given a deployer generated a password and its entry with @rafters/mail-auth-basic
  And put the entry in the list in the platform secret
  When the person's mail app logs in over IMAP with that user and password
  And selects the inbox and fetches a message
  Then the login is accepted and the message is returned
  When a mail app logs in with that user and a wrong password
  And a mail app logs in with a user that is not in the list
  Then both logins are refused with NO
  And no stored state of mail contains any of the passwords tried or the entry's hash
proves: SHALL offer a prebuilt login, @rafters/mail-auth-basic, that checks a password against a list in a platform secret
No credential SHALL reach stored state
toy 01a1a4c4: imaplib logged in, selected and fetched through the real session with a list from a binding and no credential in D1 or any state file
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A person meets this through their mail app over several IMAP commands, and the absence of credentials holds only across the whole session, not inside one unit.

checks.title: The contract suite passes a strategy that does the same work for an unknown user and a wrong password, and fails one that does not
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A strategy author runs the contract suite in workerd
  Given a strategy that supplies a counter of the work it does
  When its author runs the contract suite against @rafters/mail-auth-basic in workerd
  Then every clause passes
  And an unknown user, a wrong password and a user of 502 bytes or more each did the same work by the strategy's counter
  When its author runs the suite against a strategy that skips the hash for an unknown user
  Or against a strategy whose store throws on a user of 502 bytes or more
  Then the suite fails and names the work rule
proves: SHALL offer a contract suite any strategy can run in workerd, whose work rule is that an unknown user and a wrong password do the same work, by a counter the strategy supplies
costing one hash per attempt whether or not the user exists
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: a user of 502 bytes or more made a KV get throw and closed the session without hashing, 5 of 5; the port needs a contract clause
toy 01a1a4c4: 15 of 15 on basic, RESP and local KV, plain and wrapped, in workerd
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The suite is itself a surface a strategy author runs, and proving it means a run that passes a sound strategy and a run that fails a broken one.

checks.title: A mail app that reconnects often is not refused, while wrong guesses from one address stop at 10 in 5 minutes
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: Logins from one client address under the limit
  Given a mail app with a generated password from the list
  When it logs in with the correct password 20 times from one address within 5 minutes
  Then every login is accepted
  When, from that address, 10 wrong passwords are tried with correct logins between them within 5 minutes
  Then a further login from that address is refused, even with the correct password
  And a mail app at another address logs in with the correct password
  When 5 minutes have passed since those wrong passwords
  Then the correct password from the first address is accepted again
proves: a limit of 10 attempts per client address in a 5-minute window around any strategy, from which a correct password gets its slot back, so a mail app that reconnects often is not refused and wrong guesses stay at the limit
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: without refund a correct password is refused after 10 attempts in 5 minutes
toy 01a1a4c4 unverified claim: refund on success lets wrong guesses stay under the limit (wrong guesses under refund were not counted)
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A person and an attacker both meet the limit as a sequence of logins through the IMAP session, and the refund only shows across many logins in one window.

checks.title: Concurrent attempts from one address take exactly 10 slots, and a refused attempt never reaches the strategy
checks.rule: When 50 attempts from one address race the limiter, exactly 10 reach the wrapped strategy and the refused ones do no strategy work, because take is one synchronous transaction.
proves: a limit of 10 attempts per client address in a 5-minute window around any strategy
toy 01a1a4c4: 15 races of 50 passed or hashed exactly 10, refusals hashed 0; take as one synchronous transaction holds the race
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Through IMAP a refusal and a wrong password both answer NO, so a race that lets an eleventh guess through cannot be seen from the surface, only by counting what reaches the strategy.

checks.title: The basic check is PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations over the client's octets, shown by a known-answer table
checks.rule: An entry made by the generator verifies the password exactly when PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations over the octets the client sent matches its hash, for every row of the known-answer table (ASCII, Latin-1 and multibyte UTF-8 passwords, and an entry stating other than 100,000 iterations, which is refused).
proves: PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations over the client's octets
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: hash the client's octets; generators hash UTF-8; octets() truncates above 0xFF
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The rule is shown by many examples, so it is one table of rows, and an ASCII-only login scenario would pass with octets() still truncating.

checks.title: The basic package is MIT and imports nothing from the service layer
checks.rule: The package's manifest declares the MIT license and its import graph reaches no module of mail's service layer (cloudflare:workers is allowed for env).
proves: the package SHALL be MIT and import nothing from the service layer
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: imapObjects gives login no env, so strategies import env from cloudflare:workers
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: No user meets a license or an import graph through a surface; it is one static fact about the package.

checks.title: A real mail client logs in against deployed mail with a generated password from a real platform secret
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: Login on the deployed service
  Given deployed mail with @rafters/mail-auth-basic and a list in a real platform secret
  When a real mail client logs in with a generated password, and then with a wrong one
  Then the correct login is accepted and the wrong one refused with NO
  And the run records the CPU time of each login and the size of the secret's list
proves: SHALL check a password against a list in a platform secret with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations
toy 01a1a4c4 caveat: hashing used 5.8-7.3 ms of CPU locally against a documented 10 ms on the Free plan; deployed iteration cap, plan CPU limits and secret size unmeasured
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The plan's CPU limit, the deployed iteration cap and the secret's real size limit exist only on the deployment; this belongs on the deploy issue, and its numbers are recorded, never asserted.

gaps.failure_way: A store or the platform secret throws, is missing or hangs during a login
gaps.question: What does the client get when a strategy's store or secret fails: NO after a bounded time, or the session closing, and does the attempt count toward the limit? The toy saw EOF when the store was down and an unbounded hold when it hung; no SHALL settles either.

gaps.failure_way: The limiter's own store throws or hangs
gaps.question: Conflict between 'a limit of 10 attempts per client address' and 'a mail app that reconnects often is not refused': failing open breaks the limit, failing closed refuses the mail app. Which SHALL wins when the limiter cannot answer?

gaps.failure_way: A strategy's counter never counts, so the work rule passes vacuously
gaps.question: Must the contract suite require that a correct password shows some work by the strategy's counter, so a counter that reports nothing fails?

gaps.failure_way: A deployer puts a chosen password in the list
gaps.question: How is 'generated and never chosen' held: does the package ship only a generator that makes the password and its entry together, with no way to hash a supplied password, and what length or strength must a generated password have?
